messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: INC-6423 - Elevated 5xx rate for runtime-proxy-usw2 (detector: runtime-proxy-5xx-rate > 2% for 1m)
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty page -> https://pagerduty.example/incidents/INC-6423 (escalation policy: eng-oncall)
kevin: ack'd. looking at graphs now — pulling recent p95/p99 + kubernetes events
sara: on call handoff: i'm available if you need me to jump onto the host or run log queries
kevin: quick check: traffic steady, error spike ~02:14:28 -> 02:15:05, traces show proxy->kv-cache connection resets
anna: seeing a handful of connect errors too. snippet from runtime-proxy at 02:14:31:
```
2026-03-15T02:14:31Z runtime-proxy ERROR dial tcp 10.2.3.5:11211: connect: connection reset by peer
```
kevin: no deploys in last 30m. autoscaler didn't kick. looks like short-lived network flake between proxy and kv-cache subset us-west-2b
jess: pinging infra to check networking fabric / VPC flow logs (cc: @infra-team)
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: INC-6423 acknowledged by kevin
kevin: running a quick tcpdump on proxy host-17 to validate resets, will post logs here if anything obvious
sara: checking customer-facing errors: no increase in dropped requests in the public metrics. error budget ok. looks like internal 5xx but low customer-visible impact :+1:
kevin: tcpdump shows RSTs from 10.2.3.5 around same time window — likely a transient kernel-level reset or overloaded memcached instance
anna: memcached node 10.2.3.5 shows a brief fd exhaustion alert at 02:14:29, system logs show high accept queue then recovery
kevin: okay, that matches. sounds like transient resource exhaustion on a single kv-cache host. will cordon and restart that instance if we see recurrence
incident-bot: PagerDuty update: alert condition cleared (runtime-proxy-5xx-rate back under threshold)
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: INC-6423 automatically resolved by monitor (duration ~37s)
sara: nice — auto-resolved. still want to do a short blameless follow-up to tune alert sensitivity and maybe suppress single-host flares
kevin: agreed. quick mitigation notes: - increase memcached fd limit on that ASG, - add short cooldown before firing (30s), - add a headroom alert for fd usage on cache nodes
anna: filing infra ticket now: INF-904 - investigate fd exhaustion pattern on kv-cache in us-west-2; assigning to infra oncall
jess: pro tip: we should also tweak the 5xx alert to ignore single-host spikes by grouping by backend_host and only alert if >1 host affected OR sustained >45s
sara: assigning follow-ups: INF-904 (infra), SRE-opts (alert tuning), and a playbook note update for proxy->kv-cache flares. i'll create the tasks after this thread
kevin: no customer tickets created. recommended: watch for recurrence for 24h, escalate if sees >2 repeats in that window
anna: putting a 1-hour watch on the kv-cache ASG metrics and will ping here if anything recurs
kevin: thanks all. closing on-call loop unless something else pops up :thumbsup:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: alert cleared and incident closed
incident-bot: Reminder: if you were directly paged, please update the on-call rotation log with duration and handoff notes
sara: noted. I'll add a short incident summary to the post-incident board in ~30m (no customer impact, transient memcached fd exhaustion, follow-ups filed) :memo:
kevin: adding the tcpdump/log excerpt to ticket INF-904 for tracing. good catch everyone.
